title: Meshingress Workspace App and Source Import

origin.summary: Design a general-purpose Nextcloud Meshingress workspace app. Its first operation accepts a source URL and relative path, uses the caller tool identity to place the download under Meshingress/storage, and reports final metadata without a local Meshingress download/upload handoff.

events.note: Created after research confirmed that a small custom Nextcloud app with an OCS API route and queued background job is the appropriate implementation; Flow is optional post-import automation, not the source-import API itself.

Broadened the design from a download-only app to the Meshingress workspace app, established the managed Workspace/Meshingress directory layout, required tool identity for storage downloads, and removed EXTERNAL_EXTERNAL from the planned lifecycle model.

Moved artifacts, quarantine, and vendor under repository; clarified that Nextcloud storage is the stable official storage/<tool-id> workspace and never incorporates ephemeral session or request identifiers.
Implementation authorized: create, install, and verify the Nextcloud Meshingress workspace app.

The app is installed and enabled, but the end-to-end source-import test cannot proceed until the selected admin workspace parent exists and an authenticated API credential for a current Nextcloud user is available.
After the owner reported creating Workspace, direct Nextcloud filesystem inspection found no Workspace folder at any depth up to three under either current user, admin or temporary.

The intended workspace is on alphasunny-xps-8700, not the local AIO host used for initial installation. The ops account authenticated successfully and is in the remote admin group; its existing /Workspace was confirmed by the owner.
Resumed deployment investigation against the correct remote Nextcloud target. The remaining blocker is server-side installation access for the custom PHP app.

Remote OCS and WebDAV verification for ops succeeded, including the existing Workspace collection. Installation remains blocked because the current machine has no authorized SSH key or other server-side route to copy the custom app and run occ on the remote host.
The owner enabled Tailscale SSH and provided the remote Linux username. Server-side Docker access is confirmed; remote installation and verification are in progress.

Remote install and source-import worker verification succeeded. A brief owner-approved reload of the Nextcloud web container is still needed to clear stale web-process state before the HTTP status endpoint can be reverified.

Kept the app scoped to Nextcloud 34, added a credential-free SSH/Docker installer helper, and recorded the later Meshingress link-source storage lifecycle handoff as a distinct follow-up from EXTERNAL_EXTERNAL removal.

Installer live dry run against the existing remote app correctly staged source, refused overwrite, cleaned up, and preserved the app directory. A quoting defect found by that test was fixed; its single nested staging copy was removed after exact-path verification.
A graceful Apache reload restored OCS status-route visibility. Remote OCS now returns completed import metadata, and WebDAV content matches the worker SHA-256.

Live delegated imports remained QUEUED. Investigation found an inactive scheduler, a stale ResultAdapter::free() call in the deployed app, and MySQL NULL update rendering that blocked the RUNNING transition.
The app replacement, SQL-NULL repair, and one-minute host worker schedule are deployed. The previously queued Meshingress jobs were consumed without a new worker error.
A new delegated test job remained unrun because the generic once-per-minute worker selected from the full Nextcloud queue rather than the Meshingress job class.
The current test job was force-executed successfully. Cron now runs standard Nextcloud work every five minutes and a class-specific Meshingress worker every minute.
The owner requested removal of the minute-scale scheduler latency after validating the repair.

A registered direct worker command with one-second watch polling is deployed and running. The prior minute schedule was replaced with a boot-started persistent account worker; ordinary Nextcloud cron remains every five minutes.
The owner requested that the persistent worker become part of the app installer rather than a separate host setup.
The installer now manages one marked boot worker and restarts it after a successful app deployment, while preserving normal Nextcloud cron and unrelated user cron entries.
